text: [Liberty Surplus Ins. Corp. v. Ledesma & Meyer Const. Co., Inc. (2018) 5 C5th 216, 221-222, 233 CR3d 487, 490-491—employer's policy providing coverage for bodily injury or property damage caused by “accident” covered suit against insured based on negligent supervision of employee who committed intentional tort harming the underlying plaintiff] (b) [3:294] Compare—“claims-made” coverage: An alternative, less widely used ISO form provides coverage for “bodily injury … first made against any insured, in accordance with [applicable policy provisions] during the policy period …” [CG 00 02 12 07, Sec. I, Coverage A, ¶ 1.b(3) (emphasis added)] • [3:295] This form of coverage limits the insurer's risk to the single policy in effect at the time a claim is first asserted against the insured without regard to the timing of the damage or injury. This permits the carrier “to establish reserves without regard to possibilities of inflation, upward-spiraling jury awards, or enlargements of tort liability after the policy period.” [Montrose Chem.
